subject: anaesthesia
title: Preoperative Evaluation: ASA Physical Status, Fasting Rules, and Airway Assessment

steps.title: ASA Physical Status Classification
steps.tx: **ASA physical status classification** categorizes patients according to systemic physiological fitness prior to surgery. Class I represents a completely healthy patient, Class II indicates mild systemic disease without functional limitation, Class III denotes severe systemic illness limiting activity, Class IV signifies an incapacitating life-threatening disease, Class V is a moribund patient not expected to survive 24 hours without surgery, and Class VI is a declared brain-dead organ donor.

rows: Young adult with localized inguinal hernia
Stable angina or poorly controlled diabetes mellitus
Unstable angina or severe end-stage renal disease

steps.title: Emergency Suffix and Mortality
steps.tx: **Emergency surgery ASA designation** appends the letter E to any numeric class whenever surgical delay substantially increases risk to life or limb, such as an emergent ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm in a hypertensive patient classified as ASA IV-E. Emergency designation doubles the baseline perioperative mortality risk within each category due to inadequate physiological resuscitation and absence of pre-procedural optimization.

left.title: Elective Surgical Setting
points: Baseline mortality risk matched to intrinsic medical fitness

right.title: Emergency Surgical Setting (Suffix E)
points: High risk of pulmonary aspiration from unemptied stomach
Doubled perioperative cardiac and respiratory mortality

steps.title: Preoperative Fasting Guidelines
steps.tx: **Preoperative fasting two-four-six-eight rule** minimizes pulmonary aspiration of gastric contents without provoking dehydration or hypoglycemia. Patients may ingest clear water, fruit juices without pulp, and black coffee up to two hours prior to induction. Ingested human breast milk requires four hours, an infant formula or light non-fat meal requires six hours, while fatty, fried, or meat meals demand eight hours of fasting.

rows: Excludes milk, alcohol, and particulate juice
Applies specifically to maternal breast milk
Toast and clear tea without butter

steps.title: Mallampati Airway Classification
steps.tx: **Mallampati airway classification** correlates oropharyngeal visualization with glottic exposure difficulty, assessed with the patient sitting upright, head in neutral posture, mouth opened maximally, and tongue protruded without phonation. Class I reveals the soft palate, fauces, uvula, and pillars; Class II exposes the soft palate, fauces, and uvula; Class III visualizes the soft palate and base of uvula; Class IV visualizes the hard palate exclusively.

steps.title: Metabolic Equivalents Capacity
steps.tx: **Metabolic equivalents functional capacity** quantifies cardiorespiratory reserve: one MET equals 3.5 milliliters of oxygen consumption per kilogram per minute at complete rest. Functional capacity exceeding four METs, demonstrated by climbing two flights of stairs or walking briskly on level ground without dyspnoea, indicates adequate cardiorespiratory reserve associated with minimal perioperative myocardial infarction risk during non-cardiac surgery.

left.title: Poor Functional Capacity (under 4 METs)
points: Inability to climb one flight of stairs without stopping
High incidence of perioperative myocardial ischaemia
Mandates formal preoperative cardiac stress testing

right.title: Good Functional Capacity (greater than 4 METs)
points: Carrying heavy groceries or climbing two flights smoothly
Low risk of major adverse cardiac events perioperatively
Allows proceeding directly to elective intermediate surgery

steps.title: Thyromental Distance and Neck Mobility
steps.tx: **Thyromental distance measurement** reflects the mandibular space into which the tongue must be displaced during direct laryngoscopy. A distance measured from the thyroid notch to the lower border of the mandibular symphysis of under six centimeters (or under three fingerbreadths) reliably warns of anterior larynx and difficult direct visualization, especially when coupled with atlanto-occipital extension of under 35 degrees.

steps.title: Premedication with Glycopyrrolate
steps.tx: **Antisialagogue action of glycopyrrolate** stems from its completely synthetic quaternary ammonium structure. Unlike tertiary amines such as atropine and scopolamine, glycopyrrolate cannot traverse the lipophilic blood-brain barrier, totally preventing central anticholinergic delirium and post-anaesthetic sedation. It provides potent drying of copious oral secretions while inducing substantially less reflex tachyarrhythmia than atropine, making it ideal before awake fiberoptic intubation.

steps.title: Premedication with Midazolam
steps.tx: **Premedication using midazolam** allays preoperative anxiety through selective positive allosteric modulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid type A (GABA-A) receptors. Oral midazolam (0.5 milligrams per kilogram in children) or intravenous midazolam (1 to 2 milligrams in adults) produces profound anterograde amnesia and muscle relaxation within minutes while preserving hemodynamic stability, sparing patients traumatic recall of separation and theatre transfer.
